description: Part 2b: Write three proven verify-pantry drivers mirroring .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-stock-in.mjs - for flagged-resolution, stock-out (oldest-first consumption), and shopping-list. Each must drive the REAL user path through the web UI (not internal setters or test-only endpoints), capture evidence via captureProof (the user action + resulting state + a side-effect check through a second read-only view), and be PROVEN end to end by actually running it via pantry-verify.sh (a driver that was never executed green is a draft, not a deliverable). Use a distinct barcode and product name per driver so runs do not collide. Reuse the existing harness.mjs helpers (openBrowser, createKnownProduct, scanBarcode, captureProof, readInventory, assert); if a new shared helper is genuinely needed (e.g. scanning the STOCK_OUT control barcode, which does NOT create a card), add it to harness.mjs cleanly. Depends on FEAT-001 having confirmed the real selectors.
steps: Add a control-barcode / mode-switch helper to .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/harness.mjs (mirroring the e2e helper from FEAT-001): a function that fills the `Barcode scanner input` with 'STOCK_OUT' (or 'STOCK_IN'), presses Enter, and waits for the on-screen banner `Mode: stock_out` (getByText) - it must NOT wait for a scan card, because a control barcode returns early server-side and creates no card. Keep harness.mjs's existing exports and style intact. This is a real user action (scanning the printed control barcode), consistent with the stock-out feature recipe.

Create .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-flagged-resolution.mjs following drive-stock-in.mjs's shape. Use a DISTINCT unseeded barcode and product name (e.g. barcode '910000000002', product 'Verify Flagged Beans') and do NOT call createKnownProduct for it. Flow: goto('/'), scan the unknown barcode via scanBarcode (the card appears), assert the card shows the `Flagged` badge (card.getByText('Flagged', { exact: true })). In the card's `Create new product` fieldset fill Product name/Category/Unit of measure (getByLabel) and click `Create and use product`. Assert the Flagged badge disappears (waitFor detached / toHaveCount 0), the card now shows a heading with the product name, and a `Select scan for batch approval` checkbox appears (this is the resolution proof). Then follow the real behavior confirmed in FEAT-001 for whether the resolved entry becomes approvable: per ScanEntryCard, Approve renders only when entry.status==='pending' && entry.direction !== null. If the resolved entry carries a direction and Approve appears, approve it and confirm inventory via readInventory + the Inventory route (like stock-in). If the resolved entry's direction is null (no Approve button), capture proof at the resolved-but-approvable state and record that as the verified outcome, matching the flagged-resolution recipe's 'stop once the flag is cleared' option. captureProof(page, 'flagged-resolution', { barcode, product, resolvedStatus, ... }) after the flag clears so the ARIA snapshot shows the product name in place of the Flagged badge. Side-effect second view: either inventory (if approved) or GET /api/scans?status=pending showing the entry is no longer flagged. Print PASS/FAIL like drive-stock-in.mjs and process.exit accordingly.

Create .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-stock-out.mjs following drive-stock-in.mjs's shape and the stock-out.md recipe. Use a DISTINCT barcode and product name (e.g. '910000000003', 'Verify Stock-Out Pasta', unit 'box'). Preconditions: seed via createKnownProduct, then stock TWO instances with DIFFERENT expiry dates (e.g. 2030-01-10 and 2030-12-20): for each, scan in stock_in mode, set the card's `Expiration date` (getByLabel, blur/commit), and Approve; assert inventory instanceCount reaches 2. Then switch to stock_out mode using the control-barcode helper (assert banner `Mode: stock_out`), scan the product (a stock-out card appears), leave StockOutInstanceSelector at the default `Use oldest available automatically` to exercise oldest-first, and click Approve (exact); the card detaches. Confirm oldest consumed: open Inventory, click the product's `View instances`, assert `Expires Dec 20, 2030` is visible and `Expires Jan 10, 2030` has count 0; cross-check readInventory shows instanceCount 1. captureProof(page, 'stock-out', { remainingInstanceCount, survivingExpiry }) with the instance list visible so the surviving date is in the ARIA snapshot. PASS/FAIL + exit code as in drive-stock-in.mjs.

Create .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-shopping-list.mjs following drive-stock-in.mjs's shape and the shopping-list.md recipe, reconciled with real behavior confirmed in FEAT-001. Use a DISTINCT barcode and product name (e.g. '910000000004', 'Verify Shopping Rice', unit 'bag'). Flow: seed and stock two units (stock_in scan + Approve x2). On Inventory, open the product (`View instances`), in the SuggestionPanel click `Get suggestion`; with no consumption history it shows manual mode - fill `Manual target quantity` with 2 and click `Save manual target`, assert `Target quantity set to 2.`. Create a shortfall: switch to stock_out mode (control-barcode helper) and stock out one unit (scan + Approve), so stock (1) < target (2). Open Shopping List and assert a `Derived` badge row with the shortfall quantity `1 bag` appears (derivation proof). Because derived entries expose NO action buttons (empty id), demonstrate purchase via a MANUAL entry: in `Add an item`, select the product in the `Pantry item` select, set Quantity, click `Add to shopping list`; a `Manual` badge row appears; click `Mark <product> purchased` and assert that row leaves the list. Confirm inventory unchanged by the purchase: readInventory instanceCount is still 1 (purchasing marks intent, does not stock in). captureProof(page, 'shopping-list', { derivedQuantity, source, inventoryInstanceCountAfterPurchase }) with the entries table (or empty state) visible. PASS/FAIL + exit code as in drive-stock-in.mjs.

Prove each driver green by running it via pantry-verify.sh from repo root, one per evidence subdir: `bash .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/pantry-verify.sh drive .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-flagged-resolution.mjs flagged-resolution`; likewise `... drive-stock-out.mjs stock-out`; `... drive-shopping-list.mjs shopping-list`. Each run must print the driver's PASS line and exit 0, and write evidence/<subdir>/<name>.{aria.txt,png,sideeffect.json}. If a run fails, re-read the relevant component source, fix the driver (never fake the proof), and re-run. Because the script starts on fixed ports with --strictPort, a stray listener from a killed run surfaces as a bind failure - if that happens, wait/retry in a fresh single shell invocation.

After each driver is proven, update its feature doc to reference the proven driver exactly as stock-in.md does ('scripts/drive-stock-in.mjs is this recipe, verified end to end.'): edit .agents/skills/verify-pantry/features/flagged-resolution.md, features/stock-out.md, and features/shopping-list.md to name their driver and note it is proven, and correct any recipe text that FEAT-001/this work proved inaccurate (e.g. shopping-list's 'Mark derived purchased' should reflect that derived entries have no purchase button and the purchase path is demonstrated via a manual entry). Update .agents/skills/verify-pantry/features/README.md's Features list so each of the three features references its proven driver, matching the existing stock-in line.

Do NOT commit build/run artifacts: .agents/skills/verify-pantry/.gitignore already ignores .bin/ and evidence/. Confirm `git status` shows only the new scripts/*.mjs, edited harness.mjs, and edited features/*.md as changes under the skill dir (plus the task dir), and that .bin/ and evidence/ remain untracked/ignored.
acceptance_criteria: Three new drivers exist: .agents/skills/verify-pantry/scripts/drive-flagged-resolution.mjs, drive-stock-out.mjs, drive-shopping-list.mjs, each importing harness.mjs and driving the real web UI (no internal setters / test-only endpoints for the action under test).

Each driver, run via `pantry-verify.sh drive <driver> <subdir>`, prints its PASS line, exits 0, and writes evidence/<subdir>/<name>.{aria.txt,png,sideeffect.json} capturing the action, resulting state, and a second read-only side-effect view.
Each driver uses a distinct barcode and product name so runs do not collide.

features/flagged-resolution.md, features/stock-out.md, features/shopping-list.md, and features/README.md are updated to reference the proven drivers, matching how stock-in is referenced; inaccurate recipe text is corrected.
No built binaries or run evidence are staged for commit (.bin/ and evidence/ stay git-ignored).
verification: git status --short  (only scripts/*.mjs, harness.mjs, features/*.md, and task dir changed; .bin/ and evidence/ ignored)
